newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Generale Bank could cut Recticel to sell.
newsitem.headline: Generale Bank could cut Recticel to sell.

text.p: Belgium's Generale Bank said on Wednesday it would cut its recommendation to investors for shares in Belgian polyurethane foam producer Recticel after fundamentals showed its earnings recovery was in jeopardy.
The bank said new price hikes announced for polyoles, a raw material for polyurethane, would push up costs, slowing down the earnings recovery for Recticel.

"The good share price performance in recent days...is not confirmed by fundamentals," Generale Bank said in a note. "Further strength in the share price could trigger a renewed downgrading for the preferred share from 'hold' to 'sell'."
Two weeks ago Generale upgraded the preferred share from 'sell' to 'hold' with the ordinary share remaining a 'sell'.
Since then Recticel's preferred share has jumped to 355 francs from 300 francs, while its ordinary share has risen to 316 from 275 francs.
